Subject: SIG intake: SSO / SCIM scope and service-account details

Sean — thanks for the demo last week. Greenfield needs a short intake for our SIG submission so we can finish vendor review by Aug 18. Attached is our SIG intake form (high-level). Can you send the following artifacts by EOD Wed 8/4?

1) SAML attribute mapping examples (sample assertion with attributes you send to customers).
2) SCIM provisioning sample (example user object and a note on whether you support delta-only sync).
3) A short spreadsheet that lists any service accounts Redwood creates in customer tenants, why they exist, and the least-privilege justification (owner/team + rotation cadence).

We understand some logs are sensitive — anonymized samples are fine. If you need to schedule a short call to triage, let me know times.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz

Subject: Re: SIG intake: SSO / SCIM scope and service-account details

Elena — appreciate the clear checklist. We're on it and can deliver the initial bundle by end of day Wednesday (8/4). Quick notes up front:

- We'll provide a redacted SAML assertion sample showing NameID and the standard set of attributes (email, given_name, family_name, groups).
- SCIM: we'll send a canonical user JSON and call out whether our connector supports incremental (delta) syncs vs full sync; prod customers usually use delta for performance.
- Service accounts: we don't create persistent tenant-level service accounts by default; most integrations use a short-lived provisioning token or delegated OAuth where applicable. For a small number of enterprise customers (marketplaces/private deployments) we do support scoped service accounts — we'll enumerate those with owners and rotation cadence in the spreadsheet.

I'll attach the samples here; Laura, can you confirm redaction for the assertion sample? Karthik, can you add a line about SCIM delta window and a note on attribute filtering? Mina — please help fill the access_matrix spreadsheet with owner/team info.

Next steps:
- I will drop the initial files and a Drive link here by EOD.
- If Greenfield needs a technical call to review mapping, propose Thu 8/5 10:00-11:00 PT or 2:00-3:00 PM PT.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(sean.gallagher@redwood.ai)

Sean — looked through the assertion sample. A few redaction rules we should apply before sending to the customer:

- Remove any internal tenant IDs (sub/jti fields) and replace with placeholders.
- Keep attribute names exact (email, given_name, family_name, groups) but strip actual GUIDs from group values.
- Add a one-paragraph description at top of the artifact that explains which fields are configurable in the Console.

Karthik: can you confirm the standard delta sync cadence (we've been using 5m for most customers but some use 60m) and include whether we expose incremental change tokens in the SCIM response?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Trust & Safety Operations
(laura.bennett@redwood.ai)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG intake: SSO / SCIM scope and service-account details

Quick tech note to include in the artifact bundle:

- SCIM: our connector supports incremental (delta) syncs using "startIndex" + changeToken in Apache-style paging. Default public customers use a 5-minute delta window; Dedicated customers can request as low as 1 minute subject to rate limits.
- Attributes: we support attribute filtering; customers can opt to map only email + name for minimal footprint. Groups are synced as externalGroupIds (string array).
- Service accounts: when present we create a scoped service principal with roles limited to 'scim:provision' and 'sso:assert' for the integration; keys are rotated every 90 days by default. For private deployments we can support HSM-backed key rotation per contract.

I'll add these bullets to the Drive doc and include a sanitized sample SCIM delta response.

Karthik
Senior Infra PM, Identity
(karthik.iyer@redwood.ai)
